reason: I already pay for a change-monitoring tool that covers the few client pages I actually care about, and I'm not moving client work to something with zero reviews. I'd grab the free tier on one site and watch it for a couple of months, but I wouldn't pay anything this month, not even the $79 lifetime, because a lifetime deal from a brand-new tool is exactly what dies first.
objection: It's brand new with no reviews. If it shuts down next year I lose the dated history I was keeping for clients, and pasting my clients' logged-in browser sessions into a service nobody has vetted makes me nervous.
would_change_my_mind: A couple of months of the free tier catching real changes on a client site without false alerts, plus a way to export or download all my captures so the archive survives even if they go under.
